newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY RATES STILL LOW, SEEN FLUCTUATING.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY RATES STILL LOW, SEEN FLUCTUATING.

text.p: Dutch call money market rates remained low on Thursday but dealers said they expected them to fluctuate widely in the coming days.
Call money was bid near yesterday's 2.81 to 2.88 percent.
Participants said they were uncertain about the impact of the first expiry of the cash reserve arrangement under the new money market policy of the Dutch central bank.
"The crucial point is the distribution of liquidity among different participants," said one dealer.
He said the overall market was in balance with its need for liquidity, but individual players' position could vary.
Under the policy introduced on May 23 by the Nederlandsche Bank, banks were no longer allowed to show a debit balance at the end of the day under the cash reserve arrangement.
The current cash reserve arrangement runs until June 27.
"Call money rates might fluctuate between 2.50 and 3.75 percent bid," said one dealer.
Another mentioned an even wider range and said call money could fall close to zero and rise to a ceiling of 4.5 percent, the current rate for the marginal advance facility.
Banks have to borrow from the central bank at the marginal advances rate at the end of the day when they have a debit balance under the cash reserve facility.
The dealer added that players with a surplus of liquidity could end up with no return at all.
He said under the old money market policy, they could expect at least 2.50 percent for their surplus of liquidity.

"We are all very curious how it will work out the first time that the cash reserve arrangement expires under the new arrangement," said another dealer, adding dealers did not have much else to talk about.
"There is nothing much happening in the market," said the dealer. He said most business was done in the short-end, but added it was not much.
The Dutch central bank left the special advances rate unchanged at 2.90 percent this afternmoon, which was widely expected.
The guilder was virtually changed at 112.53 per 100 marks versus 112.535 on Wednesday.
